newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Cariplo launches rescue plan for two unit.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Cariplo launches rescue plan for two unit.

text.p: Italy's largest savings banks Cariplo said on Tuesday it would launch a rescue plan for two southern Italian savings banks which it controls.
Cariplo Vice-Chairman Claudio Dematte told a news conference that the plan for Caripuglia and Carical would involve an 800 billion lire ($527.2 million) capital increase.
Cariplo will also set up a "bad bank" to absorb some or all of the firms' bad debts which total almost four trillion lire, Dematte told reporters.
Dematte added that personnel costs at the southern banks would have to come down by 30 percent.
He said Caripuglia would chalk up a loss of around 440 billion lire in 1996 while Carical losses would total between 340-350 billion lire.
The Treasury is currently executing a rescue plan for Italy's largest southern bank, Banco di Napoli, which last year posted record losses for the Italian banking sector.
Unions and employers have said that problems with some of southern Italy's major financial institutions are stunting development in the already depressed area.

IBCA, the European credit rating agency, earlier this year downgraded Cariplo's long-term rating to A plus from AA minus, partly blaming the problems with some of Cariplo's southern Italian units for the change.
"These banks have been marred, on the whole, by poor loan quality, a lack of strategic direction and low capitalisation," IBCA said at the time.
